A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same POLAR research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original preference evaluations, downstream RLHF results, scaling experiments, ablations, and scoring case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds embedding-similarity comparisons, a pretraining-only evaluation, and separate results for reference conditions.

M1.justification: The architecture, policy-discrimination pretraining, supervised ranking loss, reference-conditioned scoring, and PPO/RFT usage remain unchanged. Initialization from InternLM2.5 and one additional pretraining epoch, emphasized in v2 Section 4.1, were already documented in v1 Appendix A.1.2.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix A reports preliminary experiments using references from other prompts with similar reasoning structures; v1 discussed this only as future work. This adds a limited reported test scenario, without quantitative results. The named training datasets, preference evaluation sets, and 20 downstream benchmarks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 adds OpenAI's Text-Embedding-3-Large as an embedding-similarity comparator. The five original reward-model baselines remain in the main comparisons. Newly cited GAIL and DIRECT are discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: The additional evaluations introduce a pretraining-only POLAR-1.8B configuration and embedding-similarity scoring on retained preference tasks. Existing data splits and PPO settings remain unchanged. Reference-free and reference-included evaluation were already specified in v1; their separate reporting does not establish a protocol change.

E4.justification: Appendix F.4 adds an ablation removing supervised fine-tuning, F.2 separates baseline results by reference condition, and F.3 examines embedding similarity as an alternative explanation. These are focused extensions; the original pretraining/reference ablations, RFT-versus-SFT comparison, scaling analyses, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that RLHF results are averaged over multiple random seeds without specifying their count. v2 adds no seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The scaling-fit statistics are unchanged.

E6.justification: New Table 7 reports average preference accuracy of 65.5% for the embedding baseline and 66.3% for pretraining-only POLAR-1.8B, alongside the retained 74.0% for fully trained POLAR-1.8B. It also adds separate baseline scores for reference conditions. Existing RLHF, scaling, and original ablation results retain their values.

T1.justification: The optimal-policy and density-ratio derivations, policy-distance definition, and training losses retain their mathematical content. The added Bradley-Terry probability formula explains the existing framework; no new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: criterion-agnostic POLAR pretraining, strong preference and RLHF performance, and predictable scaling. Their headline numerical claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning supervised fine-tuning, policy consistency versus embedding similarity, and annotation savings versus pretraining compute. The reference limitation now claims preliminary cross-prompt applicability. The motivating assertion about complementary criteria is also softened from 'always' to 'often'; the main existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds licensing and access information, while Table 6 consolidates resource requirements and adds baseline resource figures. The table reports eight H800 GPUs for POLAR-1.8B fine-tuning, conflicting with the retained implementation paragraph's 16 GPUs. Most POLAR hyperparameters, hardware details, and code information were already present.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to GAIL, DIRECT, and Direct Preference Optimization. A new related-work paragraph distinguishes POLAR's large-scale, criterion-agnostic pretraining from discriminator methods targeting expert imitation or past successes. DPO is newly credited for the closed-form optimal-policy expression.

P1.justification: v2 adds a preference-modeling preliminary subsection, rewrites the reference-limitations paragraph, moves limitations into Appendix A, and introduces ancillary appendix sections and acknowledgments. Most existing prose and the overall scientific narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds resource-comparison Table 6 and supplementary-results Table 7, relocates retained plots and tables, and places each scoring case study on its own page. Original appendix Tables 6–13 become Tables 8–15. Figures 1–10 retain their content without a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The added controls and clearer positioning improve assessability, but new inconsistencies and overinterpretation complicate the net judgment. Table 6 lists 40 million labeled Skywork-Reward-8B samples while Appendix E.1 states 80,000 preference pairs, undermining the resource comparison. Appendix F.4 dismisses pretraining-only performance despite Table 7 reporting 66.3% average accuracy and stronger reasoning accuracy than the full model. With the main evidence unchanged, these unresolved problems prevent a reliable overall quality direction.
